resources.string: This folder cannot be used. Please choose a subfolder.
No permanent access was granted for this folder.
Type: %1$s – sorted by year and month
All files in this folder and its subfolders are compared with the PC. Android asks once whether LeoSync may access the folder (needed for all file types).
Opens the Android file picker: choose a folder and tap “Use this folder”. Camera photos are usually in “DCIM/Camera”, screenshots in “Pictures/Screenshots”.
Also back up photos in folders inside the chosen folders
Copies user, password and domain. The Share path is only filled in if it is still empty.
The PC is enough, e.g. \\\\192.168.1.20. Then pick the Share and folder with “Choose folder on the PC…”. Typing works too: \\\\Server\\Share\\Folder (IP address or name).
Usually leave empty for a local Windows account. Microsoft account: use the e-mail address as user.

When the phone is connected to one of these Wi-Fi networks, LeoSync syncs automatically in the background. At least one Wi-Fi name is required for “Wi-Fi name only” and “Both”. To sync without a Wi-Fi name (e.g. via VPN), choose “PC ID only”.
In which direction should it sync?
If a file is deleted on one side, it goes to the folder “%1$s” on the other side. Off: deleted files are restored.
Keep old versions in the trash
If a file is overwritten, the old version goes to the folder “%1$s” and can be brought back via the trash. Needs a bit more storage.
Older entries in “%1$s” are permanently deleted on phone and PC. 0 = never. Default: 30
If a file was changed on both sides:
The older version is moved to the trash, not deleted.
Only while the phone is on the target Wi-Fi (at least 15). Additionally right when connecting to the Wi-Fi.
What happens to the photos on the phone once they are safely on the PC?
Files are only removed if the upload was verified (size + checksum). Android asks for confirmation once per run.
Caution: permanently deleted photos do not go to the gallery trash and cannot be restored on the phone. Afterwards they only exist on the PC.
Reads the file back from the PC and compares it with the original. More thorough means safer, but slower.
At least “Low” is required because files are removed from the phone.
Only the file size is compared. Only possible if the photos stay on the phone.
Start, middle and end (192 KB per file)
Up to 32 MB the whole file, above that 32 samples (2 MB). Default
Up to 256 MB the whole file, above that 128 samples (8 MB)
The whole file. Takes much more time and a lot of battery.
Every file is read back completely from the PC after uploading. For videos the backup takes about twice as long and uses considerably more battery.
Check set to “Medium”: removing photos from the phone requires a check.

Separate several patterns with a comma or line break. * = anything, ? = one character, folder/** = everything in this folder. If “Only these files” is empty, everything counts. “Exclude” takes precedence.
Ask if more than … % would be deleted

If more than this percentage of files would go to the trash at once, the sync stops and asks you first. Default: 20. Regardless of this, LeoSync always asks from 100 deletions at once and when a whole subfolder with more than 5 files would disappear. With at most 5 files in the profile only if all would be deleted.
The remaining steps are optional – you can already save now.
Shows what would happen when syncing with this profile – without transferring anything.
Save first – the saved state is simulated.
Forgets which files were already transferred. The next sync compares everything with the Share (identical files are not transferred again).
Reset sync status, delete profile – tap to open
Deletes the settings and sync status of this profile. Files on the phone and PC are kept.
Settings and sync status of this profile are deleted. Files on the phone and PC are kept.
What next? Until you sync this profile once, it does not start automatically. That way you can simulate first.
You have unsaved changes to this profile.
Cannot be changed after the first synchronisation.
Taken over from profile “%1$s”, which uses the same target. All photo profiles of one target must use the same structure.
The structure is fixed because files of this profile have already been synchronised. It can no longer be changed.
The structure cannot be changed while a synchronisation is running. Try again when it has finished.
Does the new folder match the previous sync status?
Is this really the right folder?
The chosen folder does not match the previous sync status of this profile. After a reinstall or an import this is expected: choose “Accept anyway”.
The next sync compares all files with the Share again. With many files this can take a while.
What should the profile be called? The name appears on the home screen, in the history and in notifications, e.g. “Camera” or “Documents”.
Which folder on the phone should be compared with the PC? All files and subfolders in it are synced.
Which photos and videos should be backed up? Choose the folders on the phone where they are stored.
Where on the PC? Enter the Windows Share and sign in with the Windows user who may access it. “Test connection” shows whether everything is right.
When does it sync, in which direction, and what happens to deleted or changed files?
When does it sync, and what happens to the photos on the phone afterwards?
Optional: sync only certain files or exclude some. Without entries everything is synced.
Optional: from when LeoSync asks first when there are many deletions. The default suits most people.
How LeoSync recognises your PC before it sends the sign-in data.
As before. Weaker: a foreign network with the same Wi-Fi name and the same address could receive the sign-in data.
Works in any Wi-Fi. The PC must be recognised before the sign-in data is sent.
Wi-Fi name and PC ID must both match. Safest.
PC not recognised yet. Tap “Test connection” once.
The PC is recognised when you save, as soon as it is reachable (with “Both” in the listed Wi-Fi).
A different PC answered. Tap “Test connection” to check it.
The PC ID is checked now: the connection is tested once.
At %1$s a different PC answers than before. Only continue if you reinstalled the PC or replaced it. Your sign-in data is only sent if you trust the new PC.
You changed the server from %1$s to %2$s. No PC is recognised there yet. Your sign-in data will be sent to that PC as soon as you continue. Only continue if %2$s is your own PC.
Please enter a number from %1$d to %2$d
Please correct the number field with an error in this step first.
Not saved: please correct the number fields with errors first.
Please enter the share path first, e.g. %1$s.
The input is invalid. Please check the share path and user.
The direction changes from “%1$s” to “%2$s”. From the next sync, the phone is the source: differing files on the PC are replaced by the phone version. The replaced version may go to the trash “%3$s”.
The direction changes from “%1$s” to “%2$s”. From the next sync, the PC is the source: differing files on the phone are replaced by the PC version. The replaced version may go to the trash “%3$s”.
The direction changes from “%1$s” to “%2$s”. From the next sync, changes are transferred in both directions.
Files deleted on one side will now also be removed on the other side (to the trash “%1$s”).
The selected folder is the top level of the storage and cannot be used. Please choose a subfolder.
Android provides this folder via a detour (e.g. “Downloads”), so it cannot be used for photos. Please choose the folder directly in internal storage.
Invalid pattern “%1$s”: a bracket is missing or extra.
Accept anyway: the previous sync status is kept.\nTreat as new folder: the state is reset and all files are compared again.

The target folder on the PC lies inside a folder of profile “%1$s” (or vice versa). The same files would be synchronized by both profiles – this can lead to duplicate copies, conflicts or unwanted deletions.

The target folder of this photo backup lies inside the PC folder of profile “%1$s” (or vice versa). The folder profile treats the backed-up photos like its own files: they can be downloaded to the phone again or moved to the recycle bin when deletions are applied.

The PC folder of this profile lies inside the target folder of photo backup “%1$s” (or vice versa). This profile treats the backed-up photos like its own files: they can be downloaded to the phone or moved to the recycle bin when deletions are applied.

A source folder of this photo backup lies inside the phone folder of profile “%1$s”, which loads files onto the phone (or vice versa). That profile can replace files there or add new files that would then be backed up as photos.

The phone folder of this profile, which loads files onto the phone, lies inside a source folder of photo backup “%1$s” (or vice versa). This profile can replace files there or add new files that would then be backed up as photos.

The folder on the phone lies inside a folder of profile “%1$s” (or vice versa). The same files would be synchronized by both profiles – this can lead to duplicate copies, conflicts or unwanted deletions.
Protects the transfer to the PC so nobody on the network can read along.
No encryption, as before. Only recommended on a network you trust.
Encrypted as soon as the PC supports it. Otherwise the connection stays unencrypted.
Connects only if encrypted. If the PC cannot do that, no connection is made and no password is sent. Most secure.
⚠ Not encrypted (%1$s). Your PC or NAS cannot encrypt, or it is switched off.
✗ Connection not possible: Your PC or NAS cannot make an encrypted connection. No sign-in data was sent. Turn on encryption on the PC or NAS (see help) or choose «If possible».
